09:00 Local Time, 03:30 GMT: After winning a crucial toss, India have been in a dominant position throughout the game. Rain has made an appearance every single day. And this is the current equation - India need 6 wickets | Sri Lanka need 288 runs. Indians coming out on top is the most likely result. The Islanders need something special even to salvage a draw. Hello everyone, and a warm welcome to the final day's play of this Galle Test.
First things first, Prakash from Galle says, “Sun and clear skies at the moment here.” But we can't guarantee that it will stay the same throughout the day.

Credit to the curator for producing a sporting deck, and it's been a nice duel between bat and ball. Batters have had success - two centurions (DDP and Sonal Dinusha) and four half-centurions (Rahul, Jurel, Dickwella and Pant) - are a testament to it. And, there's also been sufficient assistance for the bowlers - both pacers and seamers. The spinners took the bulk of the wickets in the first two innings - 15 of the 20 wickets. The seamers, however, bowled with a lot of spirit and managed to take 8 out of the 14 wickets to fall yesterday.

While the pitch may not have deteriorated as much as it usually does in Galle, batting has certainly gotten trickier with time. Sonal, just like the first innings, has been compact against spin. DdS has been anything but that. However, he's still batting and that's the key for SL. Can this duo and Dickwella frustrate the Indians? Or will it be a straightforward victory for Gill's men? We'll find out shortly.

After Pant's dismissal in yesterday's middle session, India scored only 19 runs in 8.2 overs before being bowled out. If this match goes deep, that period will be a talking point. Right then, it's action time. The players are out in the middle. Jadeja to start the proceedings for India on the final day of this Test from round the wicket.
